scenes.anchor: why does your refrigerator have to heat up
scenes.visual: The fridge cutaway (the drawing used all episode), large: cold blue contents inside, the side walls glowing orange, heat shimmer rising off them. Coil, heater, compressor and condenser stay subdued until their reveals. The question (required on screen within 10 s) types on beside it at a smaller size.
changes: cutaway draws on, contents go blue on 'refrigerator'
side walls glow and shimmer on 'heat up'
text: Why does your fridge heat up to keep food cold?
scenes.words: why does your refrigerator have to heat up to keep your food cold

scenes.anchor: it sounds backwards
scenes.visual: HERO 1 (3D). An ordinary, intact fridge in a dark kitchen, doors shut. Slow push toward the side panel. The warmth is a graphic orange overlay composited over a neutral render (the cabinet and grille must not look incandescent); the grille area gets the same overlay. A 2D chalk hand outline (composited) presses flat against the side panel.
changes: chalk hand lands on the side on 'put your hand'
side panel warms under the hand on 'running fridge'
grille glow on 'grille at the bottom'
scenes.words: it sounds backwards but put your hand on the side of a running fridge or near the grille at the bottom and you'll often feel warmth

scenes.anchor: in a hot room the sides
scenes.visual: Match cut to the same side panel in 2D (side view). A thermometer clamps onto it and climbs through the heat scale. The qualifier sits right beside the reading at label size.
text: some models, in a hot room
scenes.words: in a hot room the sides of some models get hotter than fifty degrees celsius that's about a hundred and twenty fahrenheit

scenes.anchor: that heat isn't a defect
scenes.visual: Back to the cutaway; push into the freezer. The cold coil assembly enlarges (the exact silhouette reused in S27-S29), then the heater rod just below it lights orange.
changes: push into the freezer on 'whole trick'
cold coil fills frame on 'coldest part'
scenes.words: that heat isn't a defect it's the whole trick and tucked away inside right next to the coldest part of the machine there's a second heater one that switches on on purpose

scenes.anchor: let's start with the way we talk about cold
scenes.visual: Same cutaway, door swings open. The phrase 'Let the cold out.' appears, then 'Keep the cold in.'; each is struck through while orange heat arrows flow from the kitchen INTO the open fridge. Blue stays confined to the inside.
changes: 'Let the cold out.' on 'let the cold out'
'Keep the cold in.' replaces it on 'keep the cold in'
strike + heat arrows flow in on 'no such substance'
scenes.words: let's start with the way we talk about cold we talk about cold as if it were a thing let the cold out keep the cold in but there's no such substance there is no cold to add

scenes.anchor: what exists is heat
scenes.visual: Two blocks touching, hot (orange) and cold (blue), each with a thermometer. Orange arrows run from the hot block into the cold one; the hot thermometer falls as the cold one rises.
text: On its own: hotter to colder
scenes.words: what exists is heat energy that flows because of a difference in temperature and on its own heat only flows one way from hotter to colder

scenes.anchor: a hot mug warms your hands
scenes.visual: One chalk hand, fixed in the center. A hot mug slides in on the left and orange arrows run into the hand; the mug leaves, a cold glass slides in on the right and orange arrows run out of the hand into the glass.
changes: mug and arrows into the hand on 'hot mug'
arrows hand to glass on 'losing heat'
text: the hand is losing heat to the drink
scenes.words: a hot mug warms your hands a cold drink never chills them by pushing cold in your hands are simply losing heat to it

scenes.anchor: so a refrigerator doesn't make cold
scenes.visual: Cutaway again. Orange arrows leave the milk and the leftovers and travel up to the cold coil on the freezer's back wall (not through the cabinet wall). The milk outline settles to blue.
changes: arrows from milk to coil on 'removes heat'
milk turns blue on 'taken out of it'
text: heat goes to the cold coil
scenes.words: so a refrigerator doesn't make cold it removes heat your milk is cold because heat has been taken out of it

scenes.anchor: here's the problem
scenes.visual: A slope anchored to real places: the warm kitchen (orange tint) at the top, the fridge cutaway at the bottom. A heat ball rolls down into the fridge on its own and won't roll back up. A small caption names the rule only while George says it, then fades.
changes: KITCHEN / INSIDE labels on 'kitchen is warmer'
ball stalls at the bottom on 'never go by itself'
text: heat won't climb back up on its own
Clausius statement · second law of thermodynamics
scenes.words: here's the problem your kitchen is warmer than the inside of your fridge getting heat out of the cold box and into the warm room means moving it in the one direction it will never go by itself physicists have a name for this rule it's the clausius statement of the second law of thermodynamics moving heat from a cold place to a warmer one takes work

scenes.anchor: so your fridge works like a heat pump
scenes.visual: Same slope. A pump appears on it with a lime electric bolt; it lifts the heat ball out of the fridge, uphill, into the kitchen.
changes: ball lifted uphill on 'push heat uphill'
scenes.words: so your fridge works like a heat pump it spends electricity to push heat uphill out of your food and into your kitchen

scenes.anchor: to pull that off it uses one fluid
scenes.visual: The fixed loop draws on over two zones: INSIDE THE FRIDGE (cold tint, left of a dashed wall) and KITCHEN. Stations are ghosted. One violet drop starts at the top and travels right-to-left along the top branch, toward the inside.
changes: single drop starts on 'follow one drop'
text: one sealed loop, one drop to follow
scenes.words: to pull that off it uses one fluid travelling around and around a sealed loop the refrigerant follow one drop of it all the way round and the whole machine makes sense

scenes.anchor: the trick it relies on is boiling
scenes.visual: The drop's tube section, shown twice side by side, each with a pressure gauge and a thermometer marking its boiling temperature. High pressure: higher boiling temperature, still liquid. Low pressure: lower boiling temperature, bubbles forming inside the liquid.
changes: left gauge high on 'raise the pressure'
right gauge drops and bubbles form on 'lower the pressure'
scenes.words: the trick it relies on is boiling a liquid's boiling point depends on pressure lower the pressure and it boils at a lower temperature raise the pressure and the boiling point climbs

scenes.anchor: household refrigerants boil far below freezing
scenes.visual: Thermometer with the 32 °F water-freezes line. A violet marker drops to 11 °F; 'at ordinary air pressure' sits right beside it at label size. Next to it, violet liquid in an open flask bubbles.
scenes.words: household refrigerants boil far below freezing even at ordinary air pressure isobutane one of the common ones boils at about eleven degrees fahrenheit

scenes.anchor: now the loop stop one is the evaporator
scenes.visual: Zoom out of the evaporator's place in the loop (corner locator ringed). A big evaporator tube inside the cold zone: violet liquid on the left boils into bubbles and then vapor toward the right. Orange heat arrows come down into the tube from a leftovers box, the air, walls and door. The unlit defrost heater outline sits quietly below (seed for S27). Continuity: the close-up is the left (evaporator) side of the loop rotated 90° in the transition, so left-to-right here is top-to-bottom in the loop; the same tracked drop carries back to the loop.
changes: arrows from walls and door on 'creeping in'
text: EVAPORATOR: low pressure, so it boils
scenes.words: now the loop stop one is the evaporator a coil inside the fridge here the refrigerant is kept at low pressure so it boils and boiling soaks up heat that heat comes from inside the fridge from the air the shelves last night's leftovers and the warmth that keeps creeping in through the walls and door this is where it all ends up

scenes.anchor: stop two is the compressor
scenes.visual: Locator rings the compressor. Spread-out violet vapor enters a compression chamber; a piston pushes it into a smaller space; it leaves as tightly packed vapor (never liquid) through a pipe with an orange heat halo. A lime bolt powers it.
changes: orange halo on outgoing pipe on 'much hotter'
text: still vapor, now high pressure and hot
scenes.words: stop two is the compressor the cold low pressure vapor flows into it and the compressor squeezes it into a high pressure vapor that is much hotter hot enough to be well above room temperature this is where the electricity does its main job the compressor is doing the work

scenes.anchor: stop three is the condenser
scenes.visual: Three side views of fridges, each with its condenser glowing orange: coil on the back, tubing in the side walls, coil in a bottom compartment with a fan.
scenes.words: stop three is the condenser depending on the design that's a coil on the back tubing hidden inside the side walls or a coil in a compartment at the bottom with a fan blowing across it

scenes.anchor: the vapor arriving here is hotter than your kitchen
scenes.visual: Locator rings the condenser. Inside it, one connected path rising the way the loop flows (up the right side): vapor enters at the bottom from the compressor, turns part liquid in the middle pass, leaves as liquid at the top toward the capillary tube. Orange heat arrows leave into the kitchen. The phase-change label sits beside the condenser.
changes: vapor merges into liquid down the passes on 'condenses'
text: hotter than the room, so heat leaves
scenes.words: the vapor arriving here is hotter than your kitchen so heat flows out of it into the room the easy direction as it loses heat the vapor condenses back into a liquid still under high pressure

scenes.anchor: stop four is the expansion device
scenes.visual: Locator rings the top branch. Expanded in place, flow right-to-left: wide high-pressure liquid on the RIGHT, forced through a long, very narrow bore with visible walls, out into a wider low-pressure tube on the LEFT where bubbles start but liquid remains, heading to the evaporator. Gauges: high right, low left.
changes: flow squeezes through on 'restricts the flow'
text: CAPILLARY TUBE: a long, very narrow bore
scenes.words: stop four is the expansion device in a typical household fridge it's a capillary tube a long very thin tube that restricts the flow it holds back the high pressure side from the low pressure side past it the pressure drops the boiling point drops with it and the refrigerant starts to boil again

scenes.anchor: in many fridges this tube is soldered
scenes.visual: Locator rings both the capillary tube and the suction line. Enlarged: the thin capillary (warm violet liquid) lies on top of the wide suction line (cold violet vapor); their outer walls touch along one chalk solder joint, interiors stay separate. Orange arrows cross the contact from capillary into the suction line.
changes: both lines identified on the locator on 'this tube'
heat arrows cross on 'hands some of its heat'
text: suction line to the compressor: cold vapor
scenes.words: in many fridges this tube is soldered to the line carrying cold vapor back to the compressor so the warm liquid hands some of its heat to that vapor on the way

scenes.anchor: and then the refrigerant is back in the evaporator
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full loop over its zones, all four stations lit, refrigerant circulating continuously: heat in on the inside, heat out to the kitchen.
changes: all stations light on 'loop starts again'
scenes.words: and then the refrigerant is back in the evaporator and the loop starts again

scenes.anchor: now do the accounting
scenes.visual: Energy bars, sourced on the locator: an orange bar (heat removed from inside, evaporator) plus a lime bar (electricity in, compressor) stack into one taller bar of heat into the kitchen; the electricity part keeps a lime outline so its origin stays visible.
changes: orange bar on 'pulled out of the inside'
scenes.words: now do the accounting energy is conserved so the heat the fridge dumps into your kitchen equals all the heat it pulled out of the inside plus the electrical energy it used to do it

scenes.anchor: on a tough standard test
scenes.visual: One unit scale (0, 1, 2). A lime bar of exactly 1 unit (electricity in). Below it an orange bar of heat removed from inside: solid to 1.4, lighter to 2, with a plain bracket over the 1.4 to 2 range. Electricity and heat stay separate rows.
changes: scale and lime bar on 'every unit of electricity'
orange bar grows to 1.4 then the range to 2 on 'one point four to two'
text: per unit of electricity, on a standard compressor test
scenes.words: on a tough standard test a household compressor moves roughly one point four to two units of heat for every unit of electricity it uses

scenes.anchor: so here's the missing context to the title
scenes.visual: The loop with the condenser lit on the kitchen side, thermometers attached to the condenser and to the kitchen air. While the condenser reads hotter, orange heat crosses into the room; when it drops to match, the arrows stop. Then a quick callback to the warm cabinet side from S01.
changes: condenser thermometer rises on 'hotter than the air'
heat arrows flow on 'leave the condenser'
bars equal and arrows stop on 'room temperature couldn't'
warm cabinet side callback on 'get rid of anything'
text: the condenser must be hotter than the room
scenes.words: so here's the missing context to the title heat only flows downhill for heat to leave the condenser on its own the refrigerant inside has to be hotter than the air in your kitchen that's the compressor's whole job push it well above room temperature a condenser that stayed at room temperature couldn't get rid of anything

scenes.anchor: dust lint and pet hair
scenes.visual: Condenser coil close-up: grey lint lodges in the gaps between fins; the neutral air marks thin out on the far side; the compressor run-time bar stretches longer. The cleaning card gets real space.
changes: air marks thin on 'block the airflow'
run-time bar stretches on 'harder and longer'
text: some models don't need routine cleaning
scenes.words: dust lint and pet hair on the condenser block the airflow and make it run hotter so the compressor has to work harder and longer hotpoint says to clean the coils at least once a year some models don't need routine cleaning at all

scenes.anchor: space matters too
scenes.visual: Top view, unmistakable: wall behind and beside, FRONT (door) marked. Two panels. GE: plain gap marks at the sides only. Samsung: gap marks at the sides and the back.
changes: walls and FRONT mark on 'air gaps'
text: Samsung: 5 cm ≈ 2 in, sides and back
scenes.words: space matters too manufacturers specify air gaps and they vary a lot one g e side by side asks for just an eighth of an inch at the sides samsung recommends at least five centimetres about two inches at the sides and back

scenes.anchor: and putting a fridge next to an oven
scenes.visual: The fridge cutaway stays put with its condenser at the bottom. Each heat source arrives on its word (oven, dishwasher, heating vent, sunlight) and sends orange heat toward the fridge. It ends on the S23 comparison: the kitchen-air thermometer creeps up toward the condenser's.
text: heat around the fridge makes shedding heat harder
scenes.words: and putting a fridge next to an oven a dishwasher a heating vent or in direct sunlight makes it harder for it to shed heat energy guides and installation instructions say to avoid it

scenes.anchor: now for that second heater
scenes.visual: The cutaway, freezer door opening; then the same coil-and-heater assembly from S04 enlarged (coil geometry never changes). Chalk moisture dots drift from the door and food and settle as a separate chalk-white frost deposit (thin blue edge) on the fins and tubes. The heater outline is unlit.
changes: frost starts on the fins on 'freezes'
text: moisture from food and from humid air when the door opens
scenes.words: now for that second heater the evaporator stays below freezing and the air inside your fridge carries moisture from your food and from warm humid kitchen air that rushes in every time you open the door that moisture condenses on the cold coil and freezes frost

scenes.anchor: frost conducts heat very poorly
scenes.visual: Same assembly: the white frost deposit thickens and bridges some gaps between fins. Two separate effects: fewer, thinner orange heat arrows still reach the coil (insulation), and fewer air marks get through the bridged gaps (clogging).
changes: air marks thin on 'chokes the airflow'
text: frost insulates the coil and clogs the gaps
scenes.words: frost conducts heat very poorly a layer of it insulates the coil and chokes the airflow so the fridge cools worse and wastes energy

scenes.anchor: a frost free fridge solves it
scenes.visual: HERO 2 (3D). The same frosted coil, same orientation. A lime power lead feeds the heater rod below it; the rod glows orange; frost melts back from the bottom up, exposing bare fins; meltwater drops fall. No refrigerant flow and no fan airflow while the heater glows; if airflow resumes through the cleared coil it is only after the glow ends. Camera then slides to a glass-tube heater variant.
changes: lime lead + heater glow on 'electric heater'
frost melts back on 'mounted on or just below'
slide to glass-tube variant on 'glass tube'
scenes.words: a frost free fridge solves it with an electric heater mounted on or just below the evaporator often a metal rod or a heating element inside a glass tube

scenes.anchor: while it's on it can draw about three times
scenes.visual: Title 'POWER WHILE ON', subtitle 'two service-manual examples'. Lime bars: heater example 1 ≈ 450 W, heater example 2 ≈ 470 W, compressor 120-160 W. Then a clock: the heater switches off after minutes (the main event of the last line).
changes: title and heater bars on 'three times'
compressor bar and '≈ 3×' bracket on 'compressor roughly'
clock runs and heater switches off on 'only runs'
scenes.words: while it's on it can draw about three times as much power as the compressor in the two service manuals we checked the heater drew about four hundred and fifty to four hundred and seventy watts the compressor roughly a hundred and twenty to a hundred and sixty but the heater only runs for minutes at a time

scenes.anchor: so when does it switch on
scenes.visual: One scale of accumulated compressor running time, 0 to 100+ hours. A run-time cursor advances only while the compressor runs. Older timer: a defrost tick every 8 h. Adaptive control: no event tick; a neutral chalk endcap marks the upper limit, with 'up to 100+ h, with the doors shut' attached to it.
changes: run-time cursor starts on 'how long the compressor'
text: older timer: about every 8 h of running
adaptive control: up to 100+ h, with the doors shut
scenes.words: so when does it switch on it goes by how long the compressor has been running older timers start a defrost about every eight hours of running newer controls adapt keep the doors shut and some models wait a hundred hours or more

scenes.anchor: then there's the water
scenes.visual: Side cross-section: chalk meltwater drops run from the coil down one continuous drain tube into the shallow pan beside the condenser. Orange heat enters the pan from the condenser; neutral moisture dots rise off the water surface into the kitchen.
changes: drops run down on 'drains through a tube'
heat into the pan on 'condenser's warmth'
scenes.words: then there's the water in many fridges the melted frost drains through a tube to a shallow pan down near the condenser there the condenser's warmth and in many models its fan evaporate the water back into your kitchen the fridge uses its own waste heat to get rid of its own meltwater

scenes.anchor: and there's more deliberate heat
scenes.visual: Where the door seals, up close (inside | cabinet face | door seal), two versions in turn: a warm violet refrigerant tube behind the cabinet face; then a small electric heater with a lime feed and the energy-saver switch on that electric version only. Heat reaches the cabinet face; condensation beads on that face fade and it stays dry.
text: where the door seals, up close
scenes.words: and there's more deliberate heat many fridges warm the edges of the cabinet where the doors seal either with a loop of warm refrigerant tubing or with small electric heaters the point is to stop condensation forming on the outside some models even have an energy saver switch that turns that heater off

scenes.anchor: so the box that keeps your food cold
scenes.visual: The S04 cutaway again; the explained heat locations light one after another and are numbered: 1 defrost heater, 2 door edges, 3 condenser. A recap of where the heat is, not one simultaneous state.
changes: 3 condenser joins as the recap ends
scenes.words: so the box that keeps your food cold has warm edges around its doors and a heater mounted right next to its coldest coil

scenes.anchor: all of that shows up on your electricity bill
scenes.visual: The example's identity first: 'ENERGY STAR example, 18 cu ft top-freezer'. Then its bar at 363 kWh/yr, then the dashed federal limit at 404 kWh/yr, then '≈ 10% under'.
changes: bar on 'three hundred and sixty three'
scenes.words: all of that shows up on your electricity bill the good news is how small it has become a new efficient refrigerator uses a few hundred kilowatt hours a year one eighteen cubic foot top freezer model on the energy star list is rated at three hundred and sixty three kilowatt hours a year that's about ten percent under the federal limit for its size

scenes.anchor: in nineteen seventy four
scenes.visual: Bar chart: 1974 average new fridge > 1,800 kWh/yr, tall; today 'a few hundred', about a quarter. A bigger fridge icon under today's bar on 'hold more'.
scenes.words: in nineteen seventy four the average new fridge used more than eighteen hundred new fridges use roughly a quarter of the energy of mid seventies models and they hold more

scenes.anchor: which brings us to the old advice
scenes.visual: One closed kitchen boundary. Fridge door open. A small blue region at the door (the brief puff of cold air) fades fast. Orange heat from the room enters the fridge and reaches the coil, then leaves through the condenser with a lime-sourced extra added; only after that does the wall thermometer rise.
changes: heat into the fridge on 'won't cool'
heat out at the condenser plus electricity on 'through the condenser'
thermometer rises on 'room ends up warmer'
scenes.words: which brings us to the old advice about the open fridge door leaving it open won't cool your kitchen every bit of heat it pulls out goes straight back into the same room through the condenser along with heat from the electricity it uses so the room ends up warmer all you get is a brief puff of cold air at the door

scenes.anchor: so your fridge doesn't make cold
scenes.visual: The full loop over its zones, running: three heat arrows in on the inside, four out to the kitchen (the extra one born at the lime compressor input).
changes: extra outgoing arrow from the compressor on 'a little extra'
text: plus a little extra from the electricity
scenes.words: so your fridge doesn't make cold it moves heat out of the cold box around a loop of boiling and squeezing and into your kitchen with a little extra added on the way

scenes.anchor: much of that warmth on the side
scenes.visual: The loop shrinks to the left and its condenser lights; the fridge side view takes over on the right with hot-wall tubing in the side panel glowing and shimmering: the warmth emerges at the condenser, not through the insulated wall.
changes: loop hands off to the cabinet on 'warmth on the side'
side tubing glows on 'came from inside'
text: Much of that warmth came from inside.
scenes.words: much of that warmth on the side of the cabinet is heat that came from inside your fridge

scenes.anchor: next time on designed otherwise
scenes.visual: The fridge cutaway stays on screen, warm sides gently shimmering; a small channel wordmark settles at the bottom with 'Next time'.
scenes.words: next time on designed otherwise another everyday machine that works in a way you'd never guess from the outside
